gloss: slit; incision; notch cut into something

definitions.explanation: A cut made partway into a material or a piece of food, leaving it in one piece. Used for packaging that tears open easily, for scoring bread or fish before cooking, and for notches in paper or cloth.

examples.japanese: {袋|ふくろ}に{切|き}り{込|こ}みを{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Cut a slit in the bag.

examples.japanese: パンに{浅|あさ}い{切|き}り{込|こ}みを{入|い}れてから{焼|や}く。
examples.english: Make a shallow slit in the bread before baking it.

examples.japanese: {魚|さかな}の{皮|かわ}に{切|き}り{込|こ}みを{入|い}れておくと、{火|ひ}が{通|とお}りやすくなる。
examples.english: If you score the skin of the fish beforehand, it cooks through more easily.

notes:
The noun of {切|き}り{込|こ}む (to cut into). Nearly always appears with {入|い}れる — the slit is "put into" the object.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{込|こ}みを{入|い}れる: to make a slit
- {浅|あさ}い/{深|ふか}い{切|き}り{込|こ}み: a shallow / deep incision
- {切|き}り{込|こ}み{線|せん}: a cut line, tear line on packaging

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {切|き}れ{目|め}: a break or gap — the resulting opening, not the act of cutting
- {刻|きざ}み: chopping into small pieces — cutting all the way through, repeatedly
